title: 520 MHz STM32H7P4/STM32H7P5 Arm Cortex-M7 MCUs feature Hardware Signal Processor (HSP), optional Neural-ART NPU
summary:
STMicroelectronics has introduced the STM32H7P4 and STM32H7P5, two 520 MHz Arm Cortex-M7 MCUs part of STM32H7P family designed for digital power, motor control, industrial sensing, and edge AI applications. Both feature a Hardware Signal Processor (HSP) for accelerating mathematical and signal-processing operations, while the STM32H7P5 also includes an 85 GOPS Neural-ART NPU for Edge AI inference/TinyML. The MCUs feature up to 2MB dual-bank flash, 736KB SRAM, two high-resolution timers with up to 24 PWM outputs, three advanced motor-control timers, and four 12-bit ADCs. Other features include CORDIC and FMAC mathematical accelerators, three CAN FD interfaces, USB OTG Full-Speed, and support for external memory through Octo-SPI and FMC interfaces. STM32H7P4 and STM32H7P5 specifications: MCU Core 32-bit Arm Cortex-M7 CPU @ up to 520 MHz with double-precision FPU, DSP instructions, and MPU 32 KB instruction cache and 32 KB data cache Performance – 2773 CoreMark (5.33 CoreMark/MHz) Mathematical coprocessors Hardware Signal Processor [...]

title: Olimex UEXT-CH390 SPI to Ethernet module targets Raspberry Pi and ESP32 MCU boards running ESPHome
summary:
Olimex UEXT-CH390 is a small open-source hardware module that adds 10/100 Mbps wired Ethernet connectivity to microcontroller boards through an SPI interface. It is designed for Raspberry Pi Pico and Pico 2 boards, as well as ESP32-S3, C3, C5, C6, and other microcontrollers without built-in Ethernet connectivity. The module is based on the WCH CH390 Ethernet controller and features an RJ45 connector, a standard UEXT connector, and a smaller 1.0mm-pitch pUEXT connector. It measures 50 x 21 mm and is supported in the Arduino IDE and ESPHome firmware, making it suitable for wired IoT sensors, Home Assistant devices, and other applications where WiFi is unreliable or unwanted. Olimex UEXT-CH390 specifications: Ethernet controller – WCH CH390 with integrated 10/100 Mbps Ethernet MAC and PHY 10BASE-T and 100BASE-TX Ethernet with auto-negotiation Auto-MDIX support for automatic cable detection Built-in 16KB SRAM for packet buffering Factory-programmed MAC address, eliminating the need for an external [...]

title: NXP MCX W70 and KW43 wireless MCUs support Bluetooth Channel Sounding for IoT and automotive applications
summary:
NXP MCX W70 and KW43 wireless MCU families support Bluetooth 6.x Channel Sounding for secure distance measurement in industrial IoT and automotive applications. The MCX W70 supports Bluetooth LE, Zigbee, Thread, and Matter for Smart Home and industrial devices, while the KW43 is designed for automotive applications such as digital keys and secure vehicle access. Both families feature a 96 MHz Arm Cortex-M33 application core, a separate Cortex-M33 core for wireless connectivity, up to 1.5MB flash, 256KB SRAM, a dedicated Localization Compute Engine (LCE), and NXP’s EdgeLock security features. Bluetooth Channel Sounding support combines phase-based ranging (PBR) and round-trip time (RTT) to improve distance measurement accuracy and security. title: P4 Launcher offers a PC-like and retro gaming experience on ESP32-P4 boards
summary:
Gil Tal has developed the P4 Launcher, an open-source application platform designed to bring a PC-like experience to ESP32-P4 boards with an attached touchscreen display. The launcher boots directly into its interface, while applications (.papp files) are stored on a microSD card and loaded into PSRAM when launched. You can add, remove, and run applications without reflashing the firmware or rebooting the device by simply copying files to the microSD card.Gil says 21 PAPP (PSRAM APP) applications are available now, mostly emulators and games, including Neo Geo and Atari 2600 emulators, Doom, Quake, Duke Nukem 3D and OpenTyrian, plus Clock and Files. Like ESPBrookesia, the P4 Launcher user interface runs on ESP32-P4, but it’s more flexible since it supports apps stored on the microSD card and targets mainly gaming for now. The launcher currently works on the Guition ESP32-P4 4.3″ (800×480), the Guition JC1060P470C 7″ (1024×600), and the smaller M5Stack [...]

title: 1.3 million Google-certified Android TV boxes found to have malware
summary:
You might assume that a Google-certified Android TV box will both work better and guarantee no malware. However, you’d be wrong, at least for the latter. Google has just published a new Threat Intelligence report entitled “Shutting the Door on the XCPE Botnet”, where they found that 1.3 million TV boxes were infected by the XCPE backdoor, enrolling them into a botnet used for financial gains. Google assesses with high confidence that the malware was intentionally developed, deployed, and operated by Videostrong Technology, a TV box manufacturer, which we frequently covered in the past when Android TV boxes were still somewhat a novelty and at times usable as an alternative to SBCs running Linux. Videostrong apparently monetized the backdoor by allowing affiliates to load malware modules onto infected devices to run ad-fraud schemes, enroll the TV boxes in residential proxy networks, and so on.
